name: Retrieve price and dividend data for total return calculation with all calendar days
description: Tests that the agent uses bloomberg (recommended over blp), calls history with ALL_CALENDAR_DAYS and PREVIOUS_VALUE periodicity, calls getdata for DVD_HIST_ALL, and uses string arrays
prompt: Write MATLAB code to get the last year of daily closing prices for Apple from Bloomberg. I need prices for ALL calendar days including weekends and holidays, with missing days filled using the previous known value. Also retrieve the full dividend history including all corporate actions, then calculate a total return price series. Write the code to a file called bloombergTotalReturn.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloomberg constructor (recommended C++ interface) rather than blp (Java)
assertions.expected: Uses bloomberg as the connection constructor — not blp. bloomberg is recommended because it requires no additional Java setup

assertions.description: Uses ALL_CALENDAR_DAYS and PREVIOUS_VALUE in the periodicity string array
assertions.expected: The history call includes a periodicity string array containing both ALL_CALENDAR_DAYS and PREVIOUS_VALUE — these are elements of the periodicity array argument, not separate name-value pairs

assertions.description: Uses getdata (not history) to retrieve DVD_HIST_ALL bulk field
assertions.expected: Retrieves DVD_HIST_ALL using getdata(b, security, "DVD_HIST_ALL") — NOT history(). DVD_HIST_ALL is a bulk reference data field that must be fetched with getdata

assertions.description: Uses DVD_HIST_ALL field for dividends and corporate actions
assertions.expected: DVD_HIST_ALL

name: Write full bloombergHypermedia workflow for bulk equity data retrieval
description: Tests that the agent uses the correct multi-step bloombergHypermedia workflow: create universe, field list, trigger, request, then retrieve data
prompt: Write MATLAB code to use Bloomberg Data License (Hypermedia) to retrieve PX_LAST and PX_VOLUME for IBM US Equity and AAPL US Equity. I have a credentials JSON file at credentials.json and my catalog ID is myAccountId. Show the full workflow from connection to data retrieval. Write the code to a file called hypermediaBulk.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloombergHypermedia constructor
assertions.expected: bloombergHypermedia

assertions.description: Creates a universe with createUniverse using a payload struct
assertions.expected: Uses createUniverse(b, catalog, payload) where payload is a struct with type, identifier, and contains fields — not a raw REST call or webwrite

assertions.description: Creates a field list with createFieldList using a payload struct
assertions.expected: Uses createFieldList(b, catalog, payload) where payload is a struct with type, identifier, and contains fields with mnemonic values — not a raw REST call or webwrite

assertions.description: Creates a request that references universe and field list IDs
assertions.expected: Uses createRequest to assemble the request. For reference data, the simple form createRequest(b, catalog, universeID, fieldListID) or createRequest(b, catalog, universeID, fieldListID, triggerID) is acceptable

assertions.description: Retrieves data with getData using catalog and requestID
assertions.expected: Uses getData(b, catalog, requestID, requestDate) to retrieve results — not webread or a raw REST call. The requestDate argument is required.

assertions.description: Correct workflow order: universe and field list before request, request before getData
assertions.expected: Workflow follows: connect → create universe → create field list → (optional trigger) → create request → getData → close

name: Retrieve intraday tick data with Bloomberg API flags for condition codes
description: Tests that the agent uses timeseries with Bloomberg API flags passed as two cell arrays (flag names and flag values) to include condition codes in the output
prompt: Write MATLAB code to get today's intraday tick data for MSFT from Bloomberg. I need the condition codes and exchange codes included in the output data. Write the code to a file called intradayTicks.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloomberg (recommended) constructor
assertions.expected: Uses bloomberg as the connection constructor — not blp

assertions.description: API flags are passed as two cell arrays — one for flag names, one for flag values — not as name-value pairs or string arrays
assertions.expected: Flag names and values are in separate cell arrays using curly braces and single-quoted char vectors: {'includeConditionCodes', 'includeExchangeCodes'}, {'true', 'true'} — NOT as name-value pairs like 'CondCodes', true, NOT as string arrays like ["includeConditionCodes", "includeExchangeCodes"], and NOT as cell arrays of strings with double quotes like {"includeConditionCodes"} which fail the internal ischar validation

assertions.description: Bar interval and event type precede the flag arguments in timeseries call
assertions.expected: The timeseries call has bar interval ([] for tick data) and event type ('Trade' or 'TRADE') before the two cell array flag arguments: timeseries(b, security, daterange, [], 'Trade', {'flagName1', ...}, {'flagValue1', ...})

name: Retrieve intraday tick data for a specific time window across multiple days
description: Tests that the agent uses the 3-element daterange syntax {dates, startTime, endTime} for timeseries rather than looping over days
prompt: Write MATLAB code to get 5-minute intraday bar data for MSFT from Bloomberg for each trading day from June 2 to June 6 2025, but only between 9:30 AM and 4:00 PM each day. Write the code to a file called intradayBars.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloomberg constructor (not blp)
assertions.expected: Uses bloomberg as the connection constructor — not blp

assertions.description: Uses the 3-element daterange cell array {dates, startTime, endTime} with a bar interval
assertions.expected: Uses 3-element cell array syntax {dates, duration(9,30,0), duration(16,0,0)} or equivalent with a bar interval argument (5) — does NOT loop over individual days with separate timeseries calls

assertions.description: Start and end times use duration objects, not datetime or strings
assertions.expected: Time-of-day bounds are specified as duration objects: duration(9,30,0) and duration(16,0,0) — not datetime objects, not strings like "09:30", not hours(9.5)

name: Create a historical data request via bloombergHypermedia with runtime options
description: Tests that the agent builds the full request payload with HistoryRuntimeOptions, IntervalDateRange, and HistoryFormat for historical time series retrieval via Data License
prompt: Write MATLAB code to use Bloomberg Data License (Hypermedia) to retrieve 2 years of daily closing prices for AAPL US Equity and MSFT US Equity in USD. My credentials JSON is stored with getSecret("bhapicredentials") and my catalog ID is myAccountId. Use the oneshot trigger for immediate submission. Write the code to a file called hypermediaHistory.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloombergHypermedia constructor
assertions.expected: Uses bloombergHypermedia as the connection constructor — not bloomberg or blp

assertions.description: Request payload includes HistoryRuntimeOptions with daily period and date range
assertions.expected: The request payload sets runtimeOptions.type to "HistoryRuntimeOptions" with period set to "daily" and a dateRange sub-struct specifying type "IntervalDateRange" with startDate and endDate — not a simple createRequest(b, catalog, universeID, fieldListID) call

assertions.description: Request payload includes HistoryFormat formatting options
assertions.expected: The request payload sets formatting.type to "HistoryFormat" with dateFormat and fileType fields — not left unformatted or using a non-history format type

assertions.description: Uses oneshot trigger URL for immediate submission
assertions.expected: The trigger field in the request payload references the bbg oneshot trigger path containing "catalogs/bbg/triggers/oneshot" — not a custom trigger or omitted trigger

assertions.description: Sets historyPriceCurrency to USD
assertions.expected: The runtimeOptions include historyPriceCurrency set to "USD" — not omitted or set to a different currency

assertions.description: Builds full request payload struct passed to createRequest, not simple form
assertions.expected: The code builds a full request payload struct with universe, fieldList, trigger, formatting, and runtimeOptions fields and passes it to createRequest(b, catalog, payload) — does NOT use the simple createRequest(b, catalog, universeID, fieldListID) shorthand

name: Retrieve historical data with currency conversion
description: Tests that the agent uses the currency positional argument after periodicity in the history function, not a name-value pair or override
prompt: Write MATLAB code to get the last year of daily closing prices for Apple from Bloomberg, converted to Japanese Yen (JPY). Use Bloomberg's built-in currency conversion capability. Write the code to a file called bloombergJPY.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloomberg constructor (recommended C++ interface)
assertions.expected: Uses bloomberg as the connection constructor — not blp

assertions.description: Passes currency as a positional argument after periodicity, not as a name-value pair or override
assertions.expected: Currency ("JPY") appears as the last positional argument after the periodicity string array in the history call — not as a name-value pair like 'currency','JPY' or an override field

assertions.description: Includes periodicity as a string array before the currency argument
assertions.expected: Periodicity is passed as a string array (e.g. ["CALENDAR", "DAILY", ...]) between the end date and the currency argument — not omitted, not as separate arguments

assertions.description: Uses string arrays for inputs, not cell arrays of strings
assertions.expected: String inputs use double-quoted string arrays (e.g. "AAPL US Equity", "PX_LAST") — not cell arrays of strings with curly braces like {"AAPL US Equity"}

name: Retrieve reference data snapshot with override arguments
description: Tests that the agent uses getdata for snapshot/reference data with override key-value pairs as trailing positional arguments
prompt: Write MATLAB code to get the best estimate EPS (BEST_EPS) for Microsoft from Bloomberg, overriding the fiscal period to 1BF (one year forward). Also get the current P/E ratio (PE_RATIO) and market cap (CUR_MKT_CAP) in the same call. Write the code to a file called bloombergSnapshot.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloomberg constructor (not blp)
assertions.expected: Uses bloomberg as the connection constructor — not blp

assertions.description: Uses getdata for reference/snapshot data (not history or timeseries)
assertions.expected: Uses getdata(b, security, fields, ...) for the snapshot query — not history (which is for time series) or timeseries (which is for intraday)

assertions.description: Passes override as trailing key-value positional arguments to getdata
assertions.expected: Override is passed as trailing positional string arguments: getdata(b, security, fields, "BEST_FPERIOD_OVERRIDE", "1BF") — not as a struct, not as name-value pairs with 'Override' keyword, not as a separate overrides argument

assertions.description: Multiple fields passed as a string array, not separate getdata calls
assertions.expected: Multiple fields are passed in a single string array: ["BEST_EPS", "PE_RATIO", "CUR_MKT_CAP"] in one getdata call — not three separate getdata calls

name: Retrieve reference data for multiple securities with string arrays
description: Tests that the agent uses getdata with multiple securities as a string array and does not use cell arrays of strings
prompt: Write MATLAB code to get the last price (PX_LAST), 52-week high (HIGH_52WEEK), and 52-week low (LOW_52WEEK) for Apple, Microsoft, Google, and Amazon from Bloomberg in a single request. Write the code to a file called bloombergMultiSec.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses bloomberg constructor (not blp)
assertions.expected: Uses bloomberg as the connection constructor — not blp

assertions.description: Uses getdata for reference data retrieval
assertions.expected: Uses getdata(b, securities, fields) — not history or timeseries

assertions.description: Multiple securities in a single string array, not separate calls
assertions.expected: All four securities are in a single string array: ["AAPL US Equity", "MSFT US Equity", "GOOGL US Equity", "AMZN US Equity"] passed to one getdata call — not four separate getdata calls

assertions.description: Does not use cell arrays of strings for securities or fields
assertions.expected: Securities and fields use string arrays with double quotes and square brackets: ["AAPL US Equity", ...] — NOT cell arrays of strings with curly braces like {"AAPL US Equity", ...} which fail internal validation

assertions.description: Uses proper Bloomberg ticker format with yellow key
assertions.expected: Securities use full Bloomberg ticker format with yellow key suffix: "AAPL US Equity", "MSFT US Equity" — not just "AAPL" or "MSFT" without the yellow key

name: Retrieve FRED series using fredrs
description: Tests that the agent uses fredrs (not obsolete fred), series with observations flag or fetch, and getSecret for credentials
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) and retrieve the unemployment rate (series ID: UNRATE) from 2020 to 2024. Write the code to a file called fetchFredSeries.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses fredrs constructor (not obsolete fred)
assertions.expected: Uses fredrs as the connection constructor — not the obsolete fred constructor. Look for fredrs(...) in the generated code

assertions.description: Does not use obsolete fred constructor
assertions.expected: = fred(

assertions.description: Uses series with observations flag or fetch to retrieve data
assertions.expected: Uses either series(c, "UNRATE", "observations", ...) or fetch(c, "UNRATE", ...) to retrieve the data — not a raw webread or custom REST call

assertions.description: Uses getSecret for API key credentials
assertions.expected: getSecret(

name: Navigate FRED category tree using correct argument order
description: Tests that the agent uses the correct category method signature: category(c, id, subtype) with string IDs
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to FRED and browse the category tree. Start from the root category, list its children, then drill into one of the child categories to see what series are available. Write the code to a file called browseFredTree.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses fredrs constructor
assertions.expected: Uses fredrs as the connection constructor — not the obsolete fred constructor. Look for fredrs(...) in the generated code

assertions.description: Uses category method
assertions.expected: category(

assertions.description: Uses correct argument order: category(c, id, subtype) with root ID "0" as a string
assertions.expected: Root category call uses category(c, "0", "children") — ID is first arg after connection, subtype is second. ID "0" is a string, not numeric 0

assertions.description: Accesses category children results using table or struct field access
assertions.expected: Accesses the returned category children data using field-based access (e.g. cats.id, cats.name, result.id(1), or dot-notation on the result) — not by printing raw output or using generic indexing like result{1} without field names

name: List releases and extract IDs using correct method and indexing
description: Tests that the agent uses releases(c) method (not fetch) and correct nested cell indexing for return values
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to FRED, list all available releases, and get the ID and name of the first release in the list. Write the code to a file called fredReleases.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses fredrs constructor
assertions.expected: fredrs(

assertions.description: Uses releases method (not fetch with 'releases' argument)
assertions.expected: releases(

assertions.description: Does not use fetch to get releases
assertions.expected: fetch(c, "releases"

assertions.description: Uses nested cell indexing to access the first release record
assertions.expected: Accesses the first release using nested cell indexing (e.g. allReleases.releases{1}{1}.id) rather than direct indexing like allReleases.id(1) or allReleases(1,:)

name: Search for FRED series by keyword
description: Tests that the agent uses the search method with correct syntax and knows about search options like limit and order_by
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to FRED and search for series related to "consumer price index". Limit results to 10 series, sorted by popularity. Display the series IDs and titles. Write the code to a file called searchFredSeries.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses fredrs constructor
assertions.expected: fredrs(

assertions.description: Uses search method
assertions.expected: search(

assertions.description: Passes search keyword as positional argument to search method
assertions.expected: The search call passes the search term as the second positional argument: search(c, "consumer price index", ...) — not as a name-value pair like 'query', 'consumer price index'

assertions.description: Uses name-value pairs for search options like limit and order_by
assertions.expected: Search options (limit, order_by) are passed as trailing name-value pairs: search(c, term, "limit", "10", "order_by", "popularity") — values are strings, not numeric

assertions.description: Does not use webread for raw REST calls
assertions.expected: webread(

name: Retrieve observations with date filtering and output format handling
description: Tests that the agent uses series with observations subtype, correct date format, and proper result indexing via d.observations{1}
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to FRED and retrieve monthly GDP observations (series ID: GDP) from January 2018 to December 2023. Extract the data as a table and plot the GDP values over time. Write the code to a file called fredGdpPlot.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses fredrs constructor with getSecret
assertions.expected: Uses fredrs(getSecret(...)) to create the connection — not fred(), not hardcoded API key string

assertions.description: Uses series with observations subtype for data retrieval
assertions.expected: Uses series(c, "GDP", "observations", startDate, endDate) to retrieve data — the "observations" subtype is the second argument after the series ID

assertions.description: Extracts data table using correct indexing: d.observations{1}
assertions.expected: Accesses the returned data using d.observations{1} to get the table — not d.data, d{1}, d.DATA{1}, or direct struct field access without cell indexing

assertions.description: Date arguments are strings in MM/DD/YYYY format or datetime objects
assertions.expected: Date range arguments are passed as date strings (e.g. "01/01/2018", "12/31/2023") or datetime objects — not as numeric values or ISO format like "2018-01-01"

name: Fetch data using haverview cloud REST interface
description: Tests that the agent uses the haverview MATLAB object correctly: no webread, no frequency arg, no close, token passed directly to constructor
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to Haver Analytics using the haverview cloud REST API with my API token stored in variable apiToken, then fetch quarterly GDP data (variable name GDPQ) from 2020 to 2024. Write the code to a file called fetchHaverGDP.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Does not use webread for raw REST calls (haverview is a MATLAB object)
assertions.expected: webread(

assertions.description: Does not use weboptions (haverview handles auth internally)
assertions.expected: weboptions

assertions.description: Does not pass a frequency argument to haverview fetch
assertions.expected: The fetch call has exactly 4 arguments: connection, variable name ("GDPQ"), start date, end date. There is NO 5th frequency argument like "Q" or "M" passed to fetch.

assertions.description: Passes apiToken directly to haverview constructor as positional argument
assertions.expected: The haverview constructor receives apiToken as a direct positional argument: haverview(apiToken) — not as a name-value pair, not in a struct, and not via a separate auth call

assertions.description: Does not call close() as executable code on the haverview object
assertions.expected: The generated MATLAB code does NOT contain close(c) or close(conn) or any close() call as an executable statement. Comments mentioning close are acceptable — only actual function calls to close() count as a failure.

name: Fetch data from local haver with frequency conversion
description: Tests that the agent passes frequency as the 5th positional argument to fetch, not as a name-value pair
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to a local Haver Analytics database file at C:\DLX\DATA\USECON.dat and fetch the variable GDPQ as monthly data from 2020 to 2024. Write the code to a file called fetchLocalHaver.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: File path passed as string to haver constructor
assertions.expected: The haver constructor receives the file path as a direct string argument: haver("C:\DLX\DATA\USECON.dat") or haver('C:\DLX\DATA\USECON.dat') — not as a name-value pair or via a separate open call

assertions.description: Frequency code is 5th positional argument to fetch
assertions.expected: The fetch call has exactly 5 positional arguments: fetch(c, "GDPQ", startDate, endDate, "M") — frequency "M" is the 5th positional argument, NOT a name-value pair like 'Frequency','M' or an option struct

assertions.description: Uses single-letter frequency code string
assertions.expected: Frequency is specified as a single-letter string code: "M" for monthly — not a full word like "monthly" or "Monthly" or a numeric value

name: Fetch data from remote Haver server using haverdirect
description: Tests that the agent uses haverdirect with a database name (not file path), includes frequency, calls close, and does not use havertool

assertions.expected: The haverdirect constructor receives just the database name as a string: haverdirect("USECON") — not a file path like haverdirect("C:\DLX\DATA\USECON.dat")

assertions.description: Frequency code is 5th positional argument to fetch
assertions.expected: The fetch call has frequency as the 5th positional argument: fetch(c, "CPI", startDate, endDate, "Q") — not a name-value pair

assertions.description: Does not use havertool (not available for haverdirect)

assertions.description: Calls close on the connection

name: Iterate through all variables in a Haver database using nextinfo
description: Tests that the agent knows the nextinfo iteration pattern: start with empty string, pass previous name to get next, stop on empty
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to a local Haver database at C:\DLX\DATA\USECON.dat and programmatically iterate through ALL variables in the database, collecting each variable name and its description into a table. Stop when there are no more variables. Write the code to a file called iterateHaverVars.m. Do not attempt to execute the code — just write it to a file.

assertions.description: Uses nextinfo for iteration
assertions.expected: nextinfo(

assertions.description: Starts iteration with empty string argument
assertions.expected: First call to nextinfo passes an empty string to get the first variable: nextinfo(c, "") — not nextinfo(c) with no second argument, and not nextinfo(c, 0) or nextinfo(c, 1)

assertions.description: Advances iteration by passing previous variable name
assertions.expected: Inside the loop, subsequent nextinfo calls pass the previously returned variable name to advance to the next variable: nextinfo(c, previousVarName) — not an index number

assertions.description: Terminates loop when nextinfo returns empty
assertions.expected: The loop terminates when nextinfo returns an empty result — checked via isempty on the returned variable name or struct field

name: Fetch multiple variables at different frequencies from local Haver
description: Tests that the agent uses separate fetch calls with different frequency codes as 5th positional arg
prompt: Write MATLAB code to connect to C:\DLX\DATA\USECON.dat and fetch GDPQ as quarterly and CPI as monthly data from 2020 to 2024. Combine them into a single synchronized monthly timetable. assertions.description: Frequency is 5th positional argument in each fetch call
assertions.expected: Each fetch call has 5 positional arguments: fetch(c, variable, startDate, endDate, freqCode) — frequency is NOT a name-value pair like 'Frequency','Q'

assertions.description: Uses retime or synchronize to align different frequencies
assertions.expected: Uses retime or synchronize to align the quarterly and monthly data into a common monthly timetable — not manual interpolation or simple horzcat
